title: Release Train Charter — Nested Canaries & Capacity Hedging for cross-stack runtime/console/api launches
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Define a repeatable, low-friction release train pattern that coordinates staggered launch windows across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces using nested canaries (multi-layer canary cohorts), capacity hedging slots, and automated rollback gates. This charter will produce: 1) a prescriptive schedule template for cross-stack launches, 2) an operations runbook for nested canaries and shadow traffic routing, and 3) SLO-based rollback automation and cost hedging thresholds.

Why this ticket: Recent model-impacting runtime changes created mismatched surface exposure (runtime change rolled while console feature still behind flag). We need a coordinated cadence so model-affecting changes can be validated across API/Console/UIs before wide rollout while protecting latency and cost SLOs.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- Launch cadence template with 3 lanes: Fast (hosted API only), Nested Canary (runtime + API + console feature flag staging), and Wide (global ramp).
- Canary nesting pattern: start with runtime-only internal cohort -> runtime+api limited tenant cohort (5%) -> runtime+api+console internal beta -> gradual expansion with capacity hedging slots reserved in Dedicated pools.
- Runbook: traffic-shift commands, Grafana dashboard bookmarks, PR checklist (runtime PR, API contract spec, console feature flag toggle).
- Acceptance criteria and automated rollback thresholds wired into the release conductor (latency percentiles, error budget burn, model quality drift).

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Speed vs. safety: nested canaries add steps that lengthen lead time (added 48–72h in plan) but reduce cross-surface regressions. We prefer safety for model-impacting changes; non-model infra fixes may use fast lane.
- Reserved capacity cost (hedge) vs. risk: recommending 10% capacity hedge in Q3 for high-risk launches. Finance flagged cost; proposal includes chargeback to initiative budget.

Operational runbook excerpts (for the canary nesting flow):
1) Stage 0 — Prep: Reserve capacity hedge slot (Dedicated pool tag: hedge-q3). Ensure feature flag gate exists in console and API contract has version tolerance.
2) Stage 1 — Runtime internal cohort (10% of internal traffic): monitor p50/p95 latency for runtime and cost per-token; check model-quality evals (eval-suite: regressions <= 1% on targeted promptset).
3) Stage 2 — Runtime+API tenant cohort (5% of production tenants): enable rate-limited API tier, monitor error-rate, throttling incidence, and edge latency.
4) Stage 3 — Runtime+API+Console beta (employee/internal beta): open console flows and UX checks; validate structured output changes and function-calling behavior.
5) Stage 4 — Wide ramp with step increases and capacity de-hedge triggers.

Rollback/Fail-forward criteria: automated rollback if any of the following within a 30-minute observation window:
- 500 errors > 0.5% of requests and increasing
- p95 latency increases > 2x baseline
- model-quality regression above defined threshold (user-facing accuracy/regression tests)
- cost per token exceeds pre-commit threshold by > 30%

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Insufficient dedicated capacity when simultaneous launches occur -> Mitigation: capacity booking calendar + reserve 10% hedge + fallback policy to compatible lower-throughput model variants.
- Risk: Cross-surface feature mismatch -> Mitigation: mandatory preflight that validates console toggles and API contract in staging env.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Attach budget estimate to Confluence (Aisha) — due 2026-03-17
- Finalize PR checklist and add to release-conductor templates (Evelyn / Marco) — due 2026-03-15
- Implement automated de-hedge play in infra toolbelt (Tara) — due 2026-03-29

Notes: This charter is intentionally prescriptive so that PM/Eng/Ops teams can copy the cadence template into their initiative docs and avoid ad-hoc cross-surface rollouts. If pilot shows lower-than-expected friction, we will parameterize the lane thresholds into a LaunchConfig that product teams can opt into or out of depending on customer impact.
